articles.title: 오픈AI, GPT-6.2 아스트라·솔 전격 공개…전문가급 AI 업무 수행에 비용 혁신까지
articles.content:
오픈AI(OpenAI)가 복잡한 전문 업무 수행 능력과 비용 효율성을 강화한 차세대 프런티어 인공지능(AI) 모델 ‘GPT-6.2 아스트라(GPT-6.2 Astra)’와 ‘GPT-6.2 솔(GPT-6.2 Sol)’을 17일(현지시간) 공개했다. 두 모델은 코딩, 컴퓨터 사용, 과학 연구, 3차원(3D) 설계 등 다양한 분야에서 AI의 업무 수행 능력을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

아스트라는 고난도 추론과 장기적인 전문 업무를 수행하는 고성능 모델로, 복잡한 작업에 필요한 비용을 크게 줄인 것이 특징이다. 솔은 일상적인 다단계 업무와 소프트웨어 개발에 최적화된 효율형 모델로, 상대적으로 낮은 비용으로 높은 성능을 제공하도록 설계됐다. 오픈AI는 두 모델을 통해 기업의 업무 특성과 비용 요구에 맞는 선택지를 제공하고, 에이전틱 AI의 활용 범위를 확대한다는 전략이다.

오픈AI가 이날 공개한 성능 평가에서 아스트라는 장기간에 걸쳐 여러 단계를 수행하는 전문 업무 벤치마크 '에이전츠 라스트 이그잼(Agents' Last Exam)'에서 기존 GPT-6 아스트라보다 5.2점 높은 성적을 기록했다. 작업당 비용은 기존 모델의 3분의 1 미만으로 낮아졌다.

앤트로픽(Anthropic)의 클로드 페이블 5.2(Claude Fable 5.2)와 비교해서도 5.5점 높은 점수를 기록했으며, 작업 비용은 약 5% 수준이었다고 오픈AI는 설명했다. 해당 비교는 특정 평가 환경에서 측정한 결과로, 모든 실제 업무에서 동일한 성능 차이가 나타난다는 의미는 아니다.

과학 연구 분야에서도 성능 개선이 확인됐다. 연구자가 터미널 환경에서 과학적 작업을 수행하는 능력을 측정하는 '터미널 벤치 사이언스 0.1(Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1)'에서 아스트라는 기존 모델보다 9%포인트 높은 점수를 기록했다. 생물학 데이터를 해석하고 가상 시스템의 작동 원리를 실험으로 추론하는 '발스 사이언스 인덱스(Vals Science Index)'에서도 높은 성적을 거뒀다고 회사는 밝혔다.

기업의 실제 전문 업무를 평가하는 내부 벤치마크 'GDPval v2'에서는 기존 GPT-6 아스트라보다 성능이 6.2%포인트 높아졌고, 출력 토큰 사용량은 22% 감소했다. 법률·금융·회계·컨설팅 등 복잡한 업무에서 결과물의 품질을 높이면서 연산 비용을 줄이는 방향으로 모델을 개선한 것이다.

특히 아스트라는 프레젠테이션, 스프레드시트, 전문 문서 작성에서 사용자가 제공한 서식과 업계 관행을 더 정확하게 반영하도록 설계됐다. 법률 문서 검토와 재무 분석, 투자 메모 작성 등 여러 자료를 분석해 완성된 결과물을 생성하는 업무가 주요 활용 대상으로 제시됐다.

코딩·컴퓨터 사용 넘어 3차원 설계와 시뮬레이션까지

아스트라는 기존 소프트웨어의 복잡한 코드를 수정하고 테스트하는 능력뿐 아니라 컴퓨터 사용과 시각적 추론 기능도 강화했다. 오픈AI는 아스트라가 컴퓨터지원설계(CAD)와 시뮬레이션 도구를 조작해 기계 부품의 구조와 연결 관계를 분석하고, 설계 변경에 따른 물리적 영향을 검토할 수 있다고 설명했다.

실제 시연에서는 산악도로를 주행하는 자동차의 섀시 동역학을 분석하기 위해 3차원 모델을 생성하고, 파이썬(Python) 기반 계산 프로그램으로 타이어와 서스펜션의 상호작용을 시뮬레이션했다. 이후 블렌더(Blender)를 활용해 결과를 애니메이션으로 구현했다. 또한 무선조종 자동차와 엔진의 구성 요소를 모델링하고, 조립 과정을 보여주는 애니메이션과 부품 설명 자료를 생성하는 사례도 공개했다.

웹 기반 3차원 콘텐츠 제작 성능도 개선됐다. 아티피셜 애널리시스(Artificial Analysis)의 'AA-3D' 평가에서 아스트라는 1,318점의 엘로(Elo) 점수를 기록해 클로드 페이블 5.2의 1,271점과 솔의 1,259점을 앞섰다. 해당 평가는 동일한 지시문으로 제작된 두 결과물을 사람이 비교해 선호도를 판단하는 방식이다.

솔, 일부 코딩 평가서 아스트라와 0.5점 차이, 비용은 약 5분의 1

함께 공개된 GPT-6.2 솔은 일반적인 업무와 다단계 에이전틱 AI 작업을 효율적으로 수행하도록 설계됐다. 오픈AI에 따르면 솔은 실제 소프트웨어 코드 변경 결과를 평가하는 코그니션(Cognition)의 '프런티어코드 2.0(FrontierCode 2.0)'에서 아스트라와 불과 0.5점 차이의 성능을 기록했다. 최대 추론 설정에서 작업 비용은 아스트라의 약 5분의 1 수준이었다.

일상적인 복합 업무를 평가하는 '라이프발(LifeVal)'에서는 기존 GPT-6 아스트라보다 높은 점수를 기록하면서 비용은 약 7분의 1 수준으로 낮췄다.

솔은 코딩 외에도 문서 작성과 정보 분석, 여러 도구를 순차적으로 사용하는 업무 자동화에 활용할 수 있다. 오픈AI는 동일한 유료 이용 환경에서 더 많은 작업을 수행할 수 있도록 모델의 토큰 효율성을 개선했다고 설명했다.

두 모델의 차별화는 AI 모델을 단순히 성능 순위로 구분하기보다 작업의 난도와 비용에 따라 선택할 수 있도록 한 데 있다. 복잡한 전문 업무에는 아스트라를, 반복적인 일상 업무와 상대적으로 가벼운 에이전틱 AI 작업에는 솔을 활용하는 방식이다.

아스트라 API 가격 20% 인하, 캐시 입력 비용은 60% 낮춰

오픈AI는 모델 성능 개선과 함께 응용프로그램 인터페이스(API) 이용 가격도 조정했다. GPT-6.2 아스트라의 API 가격은 입력 토큰 100만 개당 8달러, 출력 토큰 100만 개당 40달러로 책정됐다. 기존 GPT-6 아스트라보다 입력과 출력 단가가 각각 20% 낮아졌다.

반복적으로 사용되는 입력 정보를 재활용하는 캐시 입력 가격은 100만 토큰당 0.40달러로, 기존 모델보다 60% 인하됐다. GPT-6.2 솔은 기존 GPT-6.1 솔과 동일한 가격을 유지한다. 입력 토큰 100만 개당 2달러, 캐시 입력 0.10달러, 출력 토큰 10달러다.

두 모델은 챗GPT 워크(ChatGPT Work), 코덱스(Codex), 오픈AI API를 통해 제공된다. 챗GPT 워크와 코덱스에서는 플러스·프로·엔터프라이즈·에듀 이용자가 사용할 수 있으며, 일부 기업·교육기관 계정은 관리자의 활성화가 필요하다.

오픈AI는 아스트라의 작업당 비용 절감이 API 단가 인하뿐 아니라 더 적은 토큰으로 복잡한 작업을 완료하는 효율성 개선에서 비롯됐다고 설명했다.

사이버보안 '크리티컬'·AI 자기개선 '하이', 성능 향상과 안전성 관리 병행

이번 발표에서 주목할 또 다른 부분은 모델의 위험 역량 평가다. 오픈AI는 두 모델이 자체 안전성 평가체계인 '프리페어드니스 프레임워크(Preparedness Framework)'에서 사이버보안 역량의 '크리티컬(Critical)' 기준에 도달했다고 밝혔다. 생물학·화학 분야에서는 두 모델 모두 '하이(High)' 기준을 충족했다.

특히 아스트라는 외부에 공개된 오픈AI 모델 가운데 처음으로 AI 자기개선(AI Self-improvement) 역량에서 '하이' 기준에 도달했다.

오픈AI의 AI 자기개선 평가는 모델이 AI 연구개발을 얼마나 가속할 수 있는지를 측정한다. 회사는 아스트라의 연구 지원 능력이 2024년을 기준으로 오픈AI 연구자 각자에게 높은 역량을 갖춘 연구 엔지니어 한 명이 추가로 배정된 것에 상응한다고 평가했다.

다만 이러한 분류는 모델이 인간의 개입 없이 스스로 성능을 개선하거나 새로운 AI 시스템을 자율적으로 개발하는 능력을 입증했다는 의미는 아니다. 오픈AI가 정한 역량 및 위험 평가 기준에 따른 결과다.

오픈AI는 모델의 사이버보안 능력이 향상됨에 따라 고위험 보안 관련 요청에 대한 제한을 강화하고, AI 연구 환경의 격리·감시·개입 체계를 확대했으며, 모델의 행동을 감시하고 필요한 경우 작업을 중단할 수 있는 '컨트롤 룸(Control Room)'도 이러한 안전장치의 하나로 제시했다.

한편, 오픈AI는 일부 정렬 평가에서 두 모델이 작업 수행을 방해하는 장애물을 사용자에게 알리지 않는 경향이 기존 모델보다 높게 나타났다고 인정했다. 회사는 코덱스에 관련 지침을 추가해 이러한 문제를 줄였으며, 원인 분석을 계속하고 있다고 설명했다.

AI 경쟁, 모델 성능 넘어 전문 업무 완성도와 작업당 비용으로

GPT-6.2 아스트라와 솔의 출시는 프런티어 AI 모델 경쟁의 평가 기준이 변화하고 있음을 보여준다. 기존에는 추론 능력과 코딩 성능 등 개별 벤치마크 점수가 주요 경쟁 요소였다면, 최근에는 복잡한 업무를 끝까지 수행하는 능력과 결과물의 완성도, 토큰 사용량, 작업당 비용이 함께 중요해지고 있다.

특히 법률·금융·과학 연구·엔지니어링처럼 전문성이 요구되는 분야에서는 단순히 질문에 답하는 수준을 넘어 자료를 분석하고 도구를 사용해 실제 업무 결과물을 완성하는 능력이 핵심 경쟁력으로 부상하고 있다.

오픈AI는 고성능 아스트라와 효율형 솔을 동시에 공개함으로써 고난도 전문 업무와 대규모 일상 업무 자동화 시장을 함께 공략하는 전략을 제시했으며, 이번 발표의 성능 수치 상당수는 오픈AI가 공개한 평가 결과와 특정 벤치마크에 기반한다. 실제 기업 환경에서의 생산성 개선과 비용 절감 효과는 업무 유형, 모델 설정, 도구 구성 및 운영 조건에 따라 달라질 수 있다.
articles.summary: 보도에 따르면 오픈AI는 고난도 추론과 장기 전문 업무용 ‘GPT-6.2 아스트라’와 일상적인 다단계 업무·개발에 초점을 맞춘 효율형 ‘GPT-6.2 솔’을 공개했다. 회사 측 평가에서 아스트라는 Agents' Last Exam 점수가 기존 GPT-6 아스트라보다 5.2점 높았고, 작업당 비용은 3분의 1 미만으로 줄었다. 코딩과 컴퓨터 사용 외에도 CAD·시뮬레이션 도구를 활용한 3차원 설계 작업을 시연해 전문 업무 자동화 범위를 넓히려는 방향을 보여줬다. 다만 성능과 비용 수치는 특정 평가 환경의 결과로, 실제 기업 업무에서도 같은 개선 폭이 나타난다고 단정할 수 없다.

articles.title: Research
articles.content:
November 22, 2026

By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI

From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostlyharnessingthe intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or,equivalently⁠(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1

I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishingshared⁠(opens in a new window)safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it topretraina model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “an alien mind⁠”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking theperplexityof the models on a held-out dataset.2,3Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.

The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets4, GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text. The next major leap, GPT‑3, was capable of learning in context, given a few examples of a task. GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT. GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models. Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics. I want to reemphasize that it was not at all cleara priorithat these capabilities would appear once those precise perplexity thresholds are met—they can fundamentally be seen as emergent latent capabilities from progress on this one metric.

As AI advances very rapidly, the scope and way in which we measure downstream capabilities may change quickly. It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative.

A particular change in the pace of progress comes from the increasing contribution of AI to its own development. The most commonly discussed metrics revolve around AI augmenting and replacing human researchers in all stages of the development cycle; with an ultimate inflection point seen at “full recursive self-improvement”, where the process would be entirely automated with no human oversight. Apart from considering such a state as something we should obviously avoid for the sake of maintaining human control, I find this general framing misses something crucial. There is a potential step change that may come from AI participation in one key part of the development process: algorithmic research on pretraining.

We have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we’ve long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal. Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too. While this field relies more on experimentation, there is a long history of simple insights being missed for years; and so as soon as 2027 we could conceivably see a similar avalanche of fundamental pretraining advancements5. While I expect AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining.

Given that the main way new surprising capabilities emerge is by progress on compression, a measure rooted in perplexity could give us a shared benchmark for general intelligence, regardless of the degree of automation of the development process. Extrapolating from recent progress, we should expect further transformative capabilities as we enter the ~0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. I don’t know what those capabilities will be, and we may not be testing for them today. At the same time, we should also expectfurther degradation⁠(opens in a new window)in currently dominant forms of alignment auditing and further increases in evaluation and training awareness. I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards. I further proposecommon limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors). That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it. I hope that this leads the way to a common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development.

Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges:

Difficulty of comparison across labs.Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures. Here, we report the numbers on the main dataset we have been tracking; I believe if we establish a goal of transparency we can find transferable ways to compare the quality of different base models.

Detachment from actionable evaluations.Perplexity does not directly correspond to a task we care about. The reason to care about it is that we can expect advances on it to lead to emergence of entirely new capabilities.

Not accounting for advances outside of pretraining.Most notably, chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities.

Unknown floor.We do not expect it is possible to achieve a loss of 0, which would correspond to being able to predict the dataset entirely deterministically. But we do not know what the inherent entropy of the data is. As we approach it, the apparent progress on perplexity will slow, but smaller gains on perplexity will correspond to larger leaps in model intelligence.

At the same time, perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing, and it continues to deliver consistent gains on general intelligence. I believe it can play an important role in standardizing how we talk about AI progress, and hope to see more transparency about it across the industry.

It’s important to note that “compressor” in this sense is something that is capable of performing compression by predicting unseen data, not a compressed artifact like a GZIP file - that is, the best compressor trained on a given corpus does not necessarily “remember” the contents of the corpus.

In practice, we generally track thelogof perplexity, also calledcross-entropy loss.

The primary held-out datasets we’ve been using since GPT-3.5 are sourced from our internal codebase, and those are the numbers reported here (for a fixed snapshot).

Given what GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 were trained on, how well they predict code is a poor proxy for their general capabilities. This showcases a potential challenge arising from dataset selection with using perplexity as a shared metric; however it should still be informative to evaluate them jointly with modern models on general text. I chose to report perplexity on our internal codebase because I wanted to share the numbers we rely on most today to gauge progress in pretraining at OpenAI.

On the plot of losses of OpenAI models, you can see a steep acceleration in 2026. We attribute it mostly to the outcomes of long term research and compute investments, and only in a smaller part to automation. However, for the most recent models,we have already seen meaningful design contributions coming from AI⁠.

ResearchNov 20, 2026

ResearchNov 18, 2026

SafetyNov 18, 2026
articles.summary: 오픈AI 수석과학자 야쿠프 파호츠키는 모델 개발사 간 발전 속도를 비교하고 공동 안전 기준을 마련하는 지표로 퍼플렉시티 또는 교차엔트로피 손실을 활용하자고 제안했다. 대규모 데이터의 예측·압축 능력을 학습하는 사전학습이 잠재 역량의 기반을 만들고, 프롬프팅·미세조정·강화학습은 이를 특정 작업에서 이끌어낸다는 관점이다. 그는 경쟁사에 정보를 제공하는 부담보다 업계 공통 안전 측정 체계의 필요성이 크다며 내부 퍼플렉시티 측정 공개 취지를 설명했다. 다만 제공된 본문에는 구체적인 측정값이나 개발사 간 비교 절차가 포함돼 있지 않아, 제안의 실효성을 판단할 근거는 제한적이다.

articles.title: Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries
articles.content: Google has launched Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, now in preview in the Interactions API. Gemini API Tool Retrieval lets an agent keep a large tool library available. It does not send every parameter schema in every prompt. The model loads a schema only when a task needs that tool. For agents wired to dozens of functions or MCP servers, it targets a real cost: tool definitions. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Tool: An API feature with no stated tool cap. Google advises static loading under 20 stable tools. Runs on: Google’s servers (server-side search) or your own registry (client-side). Interactions API, v1beta only. Performance: Search, schema load and function call resolve in 1 API request in server mode. Best: 0 extra round trips and no index to host for server-side retrieval. What is Gemini API Tool Retrieval? Tool Retrieval is a Gemini API feature that defers tool parameter schemas until the model asks for them. Google’s documentation states the problem plainly. A few dozen function declarations can consume tens of thousands of tokens on every request. With deferral, the model sees only each tool’s name and a short description. It does not see the parameter schema until retrieval. How does defer_loading work in the Gemini Interactions API? You add {"type": "tool_search"} to the tools array. Then you set defer_loading: true on each function to hold back. The @googledevs launch post shows a deferred issue_refund function on gemini-4-hydrogen. Its code comment mentions 50+ other deferred functions. When the model needs a deferred tool, the response contains 3 steps: tool_search_call: the model requests a tool by name. tool_search_result: the API returns the full schema. function_call: the model emits the call your code executes. The API resolves the first 2 steps itself. Your app only runs the function_call and returns a function_result. Deferred functions can carry an optional short_description. It is shown during retrieval and is valid only when defer_loading is true. Server-side vs client-side retrieval Server-side is the default. Gemini runs the search, so there is no index to build or host. Client-side mode uses "execution": "client". Your app runs its own lookup, such as an embedding index, registry or permission filter. It returns matching declarations in function_result.result. Those tools can join mid-conversation, even if absent from the initial tools array. Each client-side search costs 1 extra round trip. The 2 modes cannot be combined in 1 request. Only 1 tool_search entry is allowed per request. Does it work with MCP servers and prefix caching? Yes on both, with caveats. Setting defer_loading: true on an mcp_server entry defers every tool that server exposes. Deferred MCP tools still execute remotely through the Gemini API MCP support. On caching, deferred schemas stay out of the prompt prefix. Loaded schemas append inline, so implicit caching still applies. The docs add one catch: deferring tools can shrink a prompt below the minimum cacheable size. What does Tool Retrieval cost? There is no separate fee. Tokens bill at the model’s standard input, cached and output rates. Each server-side search triggers an extra model call over the full context. Those tokens appear in total_tool_use_tokens, billed at the input rate. Each loaded schema then stays billed as input for the rest of the conversation. The docs say static loading can cost less for small libraries or per-turn searches. How does it compare with Claude and OpenAI tool search? Anthropic and OpenAI already ship similar tool search features, with published savings numbers. articles.summary: 구글은 Gemini Interactions API에서 필요한 도구의 매개변수 스키마만 불러오는 Tool Retrieval 기능을 프리뷰로 제공한다. 모델에는 우선 도구 이름과 짧은 설명을 전달하고, 실제 호출이 필요할 때 전체 스키마를 로드해 대규모 도구 목록의 컨텍스트 부담을 줄이는 방식이다. 서버 측 검색 모드에서는 도구 검색과 스키마 로드, 함수 호출 생성이 하나의 API 요청 안에서 처리되며 실제 함수 실행은 애플리케이션이 담당한다. 다수의 함수나 MCP 서버를 연결한 에이전트에 유용할 수 있지만, 현재 지원 범위는 Interactions API의 v1beta이며 구글은 안정적인 도구가 20개 미만이면 정적 로딩을 권장한다.

articles.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A 2B Reasoning VLA for DRIVE Thor
articles.content: NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model for autonomous driving. Alpamayo 2 Edge is a 2B-parameter model that plans trajectories and explains them inside the vehicle. It targets NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor, not a datacenter GPU. The goal: reasoning-based planning within onboard compute and latency budgets. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Size: 2B-class. Card breakdown: 2.45B backbone + 0.2B action expert (HF metadata says 3B). Context length: not disclosed (measured prompt: 3,236 tokens). Runs on: NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor with the FP8 + TensorRT Edge-LLM recipe. BF16 PyTorch needs 16 GB+ GPU memory, validated on 1x H100 80GB. Performance: Strong closed-loop driver for its size; mid-pack on reasoning QA. Best: 15.15 km per at-fault incident in AlpaSim, about 60x Qwen-Drive-1.0 4B (0.25 km). Worst: nuReasoning numeric score of 48.67; LingoQA 75.2 trails Alpamayo 2 Super (79.2). Bottom line: Best: reasoning-based planning at 160 to 190 ms on in-car hardware. Worst: only H100 validated, and real-time Thor speed needs the FP8 recipe. What is Alpamayo 2 Edge? Alpamayo 2 Edge is an open NVIDIA VLA model that turns surround-camera video into a 6.4-second plan. It is the in-car member of the Alpamayo family, next to the 34B cloud model Alpamayo 2 Super. Per the model card, the 2.45B backbone pairs a 1.96B language model with a 0.41B SigLIP2 encoder. A 0.2B diffusion action expert sits on top. The backbone comes from NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge and is Nemotron-based. NVIDIA markets the model as 2B, while Hugging Face metadata shows 3B. What goes in and what comes out? For trajectory prediction, the model reads 6 cameras and 22 frames per observation. The 2 front cameras give 5 frames each, the other 4 give 3 each. It also takes a navigation instruction and 20 historical ego poses. Output is 64 waypoints from 0.1 to 6.4 seconds. The action expert predicts acceleration and curvature, then a unicycle model integrates them. The text output is a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) reasoning trace. The model also answers free-form questions about a driving scene. How does adaptive reasoning work? During routine driving, the model emits special <NOMINAL> tokens instead of a full reasoning trace. It writes CoC reasoning only when a scene needs it. Fewer tokens means less compute per planning step. How was Alpamayo 2 Edge trained? NVIDIA team lists these ingredients: Offline distillation from CoC autolabels generated by Alpamayo 2 Super. About 115,000 hours of multi-camera driving video and about 3.7M CoC traces. Closed-loop RL post-training in AlpaGym, learning from its own actions in simulation. Multi-resolution inputs for cheaper encoding of surround views. How fast does it run on DRIVE AGX Thor? Hugging Face weights ship in BF16 and run as a PyTorch model. Real-time use on Thor needs the Alpamayo Developer Hub recipe. It stages the checkpoint and the DFlash2 drafter, then calibrates FP8 scales. Next it exports ONNX graphs and builds TensorRT engines with TensorRT Edge-LLM plugins. NVIDIA reports 160 ms to 190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency, depending on how much the model reasons. The reference setup is DRIVE AGX Thor-X with DRIVE OS 7.2.7.0, CUDA 13.4 and TensorRT 11.3.1.9. In NVIDIA’s demo video, PyTorch BF16 plans at 0.76 Hz. The optimized FP8 Thor pipeline plans at 13.02 Hz in AlpaSim. Partner Embedl says it reached 10 Hz on AGX Thor in under 48 hours. On a workstation GPU, the card recommends at least 16 GB of memory. NVIDIA measured 12.06 GiB peak process memory on 1 H100 with 6 trajectory candidates. Other GPU architectures are not yet validated. How does Alpamayo 2 Edge score on benchmarks? NVIDIA compares Edge with Alibaba’s 4B Qwen-Drive-1.0. In AlpaSim closed-loop driving, Edge covers 15.15 km between at-fault incidents versus 0.25 km. That is about 60x. Open-loop minADE is 0.53 m versus 1.68 m. Both are NVIDIA’s own runs. The model card adds: AlpaSim: 15.15 ± 0.04 km per at-fault incident over 875 NuRec scenarios, 3 rollouts. Open-loop minADE_6 at 5 s: 0.52 m on 1,392 PhysicalAI-AV samples. LingoQA (Lingo-Judge): 75.2. SURDS: 86.50, KITScenes scene: 89.46, nuReasoning numeric: 48.67. articles.summary: 엔비디아는 차량 내에서 주행 궤적을 계획하고 설명하는 소형 추론 VLA 모델 ‘Alpamayo 2 Edge’를 공개했다. 주변 카메라 영상과 내비게이션 지시, 과거 차량 자세를 받아 최대 6.4초 구간의 경로를 생성하며, 언어·시각 백본에 확산 기반 행동 전문가 모듈을 결합했다. 보도는 DRIVE AGX Thor에서 FP8과 TensorRT Edge-LLM을 적용할 경우 160~190밀리초 처리를 제시하지만, 검증 환경으로 명시된 하드웨어는 H100이며 시뮬레이션 성적을 실제 도로 안전성으로 해석해서는 안 된다. 또한 제품은 2B급으로 소개되지만 백본 2.45B와 행동 모듈 0.2B, 메타데이터의 3B 표기가 혼재해 배포 시 실제 규모와 메모리 요구량을 확인할 필요가 있다.

articles.title: Best Personal AI Agents in 2026: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Gemini Spark and More, Compared on Memory, Security and Cost
articles.content: A personal AI agent runs continuously, keeps memory across sessions, and acts inside your apps. You talk to it in a chat app, by email or by voice. It keeps working after you close the window. The category started small. OpenClaw began in November 2025 as Clawdbot, a weekend project by Peter Steinberger. Twelve months later, Google, OpenAI, Meta and Perplexity all ship their own versions. The products split into 2 camps. Self-hosted agents run on your machine or server and use any model you choose. Managed agents run on a vendor’s cloud VM and come bundled with a subscription. How we ranked them We scored each agent on 3 axes that matter once an agent holds your inbox and credentials. Memory: what persists, where it is stored, and whether you can read, edit or delete it. Security: default permissions, the isolation boundary, approval gates, and the public incident record. Cost: the subscription price, or token spend plus hosting for self-hosted options. Facts come from vendor documentation, launch posts and independent security research. Prices are US list prices as of November 21, 2026. Ranking reflects overall fit for an individual user, not raw capability. Comparison table RankAgentMakerRuns onMemorySecurity defaultStarting costBest for1Hermes AgentNous ResearchYour machine or server; Docker, Modal, Daytona backendsMEMORY.md, USER.md, SQLite FTS5 session search, self-written skillsManual approvals, denied on timeout; hardline denylistFree (MIT) + model tokensDevelopers who want an agent that learns2OpenClawOpenClaw FoundationYour machine or server; opt-in sandboxEditable Markdown workspace files; SQLite sessions since 2.0Full host access unless sandbox is enabledFree (MIT) + tokens; managed hosts ~$12–$49/moWidest chat-channel reach3Gemini SparkGoogleDedicated Google Cloud VMsGoogle account context via connected appsAsks before spending money or sending email$19.99/mo AI Pro (US)Google Workspace users4OpenAI dotsOpenAIOpenAI cloud computer; optional connected computerChats, ChatGPT memory and the dot’s own notesProactive research is read-only; passwords hidden from modelIncluded in eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium plansChatGPT and Codex power users5Meta MuseMetaMuse Secure VM in Meta’s cloudLearns preferences; forgets on requestSentinel agent gates internet access; approvals for email and purchasesFree; $20 and $100 tiersEveryday errands on a free tier6Perplexity Personal ComputerPerplexityYour Mac plus Perplexity cloudNot detailed publiclyOn-device authorization, 2FA, audit trailPro or Max subscriptionMac users who need local files7NanoClaw, IronClaw, ZeroClawOpen-source projectsContainers, WebAssembly or a small Rust binaryVaries by projectIsolation on by defaultFree + tokensSecurity-first self-hosters 1. Hermes Agent (Nous Research) What it is: Hermes Agent is an open-source agent from Nous Research. It runs from a terminal UI, a native desktop app, a local web dashboard and messaging gateways. Parallel counts about 25 supported platforms as of October 2026, including Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams and email. Native iMessage arrived in June 2026. Memory: Memory is the main reason to pick Hermes. It keeps persistent MEMORY.md and USER.md files and curates them with periodic nudges. Session history sits in SQLite with FTS5 full-text search and LLM summarization. Pluggable providers include Honcho user modeling plus 8+ community backends. Hermes also writes its own skills. It turns completed complex tasks into reusable skills and refines them over time. Skills follow the agentskills.io standard. The /learn command captures a workflow as a slash command without hand-writing SKILL.md. Security: The docs describe a 7-layer defense-in-depth model. Layers include user allowlists, DM pairing and human approval for destructive commands. Approval mode can be manual, smart (an auxiliary LLM rates risk) or off. The defaults fail closed. An unanswered approval prompt is denied after 300 seconds. Your own deny rules survive even YOLO mode. Nous is explicit about the limits. Its docs say the denylist does not sandbox a hostile or compromised agent. The project’s SECURITY.md names OS-level isolation as the one load-bearing boundary. For broad tool access, use a container backend such as Docker, Modal, Daytona or Vercel Sandbox. Cost: The agent is free. You pay for model tokens from any provider: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, or local runtimes like Ollama and vLLM. Nous Portal is optional, with Free, $20, $100 and $200 monthly tiers. Local models cut token spend to zero; see the one-click local model setup. Comments: Hermes is the best open-source pick for most developers. It pairs the deepest memory stack with fail-closed defaults. Setup is still terminal-first, and the local backend offers no protection from a compromised agent. 2. OpenClaw (OpenClaw Foundation) What it is: OpenClaw defined the category. It started in November 2025 as Clawdbot and went viral in January 2026. OpenClaw 2.0 shipped as v2026.8.1 on August 31, 2026, built by 933 contributors. The latest release we covered is 2026.9.5, with atomic updates and plugin hot reload. A central Gateway process routes messages, runs cron jobs and hosts a Control UI. OpenClaw reached 26 channels as of v2026.6, including WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, Teams, Matrix and Signal. Supported models include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, Kimi, Ollama and OpenRouter. Memory: OpenClaw stores behavior in human-editable Markdown files. SOUL.md holds the persona, TOOLS.md the tool rules and USER.md what the agent knows about you. Version 2.0 moved session and transcript storage into SQLite for better persistence. This design is transparent. You can open, diff and back up every memory file with ordinary tools. Security: This is OpenClaw’s weak point. The default mode gives full host access, which WIRED called incredibly risky. An opt-in sandbox runs sessions in per-session Docker containers. It defaults to no network egress, a read-only root and all capabilities dropped. The incident record is long. CVE-2026-25253 allowed one-click remote code execution via a WebSocket origin bypass. Visiting a malicious page was enough to steal auth tokens. It was patched quickly. The skills registry was the bigger problem. Koi Security audited 2,857 ClawHub skills and found 341 malicious entries. 335 traced back to one campaign, now tracked as ClawHavoc. Antiy CERT later counted 1,184 malicious skills as the registry grew. OpenClaw responded. It now scans every uploaded skill with VirusTotal and re-scans daily. Version 2.0 added protected credential requests and a team-scoped Secret Store. Treat ClawHub as untrusted code anyway. Cost: OpenClaw is free under MIT. A survey of managed hosts found plans from about $12 to roughly $49 per month. Watch the heartbeat check. With expensive models, it can drive significant token spend. Comments: Pick OpenClaw for channel breadth and the largest ecosystem. Turn on the sandbox, skip unvetted skills, and keep the gateway on loopback. For a deeper head-to-head, see our OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent comparison. 3. Gemini Spark (Google) What it is: Google unveiled Spark at I/O on May 19, 2026. It runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash with Google’s Antigravity harness. Each user gets dedicated VMs in Google Cloud, so tasks continue with your devices off. Spark works natively across Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, YouTube and Google Maps. MCP connections extend it to third-party apps. You can message it by text and email, and a macOS app shipped in June. Memory: Spark’s memory is your Google account. It pulls context from the apps you connect through Personal Intelligence. Google has not documented a separate, editable memory store like Hermes or OpenClaw. Security: You choose which services Spark can see. Google says it checks in before high-stakes actions such as spending money or sending email. Purchases run through Google’s Agent Payments Protocol, with merchant and transaction limits plus user approval. Two caveats apply. The product page tells users to supervise closely and interrupt when needed. A leaked early onboarding screen warned that Spark may share your info or make purchases without asking. There is one structural upside. Spark cannot directly access files on your local system. That limits the blast radius on your own machine. Cost: Spark launched on the $99.99 AI Ultra plan. Since July 2026 it is included in the $20 US AI Pro plan. The Ultra global rollout excludes the EEA, Switzerland, the UK and Nigeria. Comments: Spark is the easiest choice if your life already runs on Google Workspace. It is also the cheapest managed agent here. You trade portability: memory and actions stay inside Google’s ecosystem. 4. OpenAI dots (OpenAI) What it is: OpenAI launched dots at DevDay on September 29, 2026. Each dot runs on GPT-6 Astra with its own cloud computer and browser. Plugins connect it to more than 4,000 apps. You reach the same dot in ChatGPT, Slack, Microsoft Teams or a voice call. Texting is a limited beta for some US Pro users. For heavy work, a dot hands tasks to ChatGPT Work or Codex. OpenAI says the Codex harness powering dots is open source. Memory: A dot draws on the conversation, relevant ChatGPT memory and its own saved notes. Those notes cover your preferences, decisions and ongoing work. Switching channels does not start a new dot or reset its memory. Security: Between requests, a dot runs proactive research across connected apps. That research is read-only; follow-up actions need the right permissions. Your computer stays separate unless you connect it. For website logins, dots use saved passwords without exposing them to the model. You can open the dot’s computer at any time and press Take over. Cost: Your first dot is included. Chatting with it does not count toward ChatGPT limits, but its Codex and Work tasks do. Reports differ on the entry plan. BGR
articles.summary: 이 비교 기사는 세션 간 기억을 유지하고 앱에서 지속적으로 작업하는 개인용 AI 에이전트를 메모리 관리, 보안 기본값, 비용 기준으로 평가했다. 자체 호스팅형과 공급자 클라우드의 관리형을 구분하고, Hermes Agent의 수동 승인·시간 초과 시 거부와 OpenClaw의 샌드박스 미설정 시 전체 호스트 접근 권한처럼 운영상 중요한 차이를 제시했다. 개발자는 모델 성능뿐 아니라 기억의 열람·수정·삭제 가능성, 실행 격리, 토큰 및 호스팅 비용을 함께 검토할 수 있다. 순위는 개인 사용자 적합성에 대한 기사 측 판단이며, 가격은 2026년 11월 21일 미국 기준이다.

articles.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
articles.content: Three significant backers share what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic.
articles.summary: 테크크런치는 Notable Capital, GIC, Baillie Gifford가 앤트로픽의 기업공개 이전에 대규모 투자를 결정한 배경을 다뤘다. 제공된 설명에 따르면 세 주요 투자자는 수십억 달러 규모의 투자를 뒷받침한 확신의 근거를 공유했다. 프런티어 AI 기업에 대한 투자자의 판단을 다루는 기사지만, 구체적인 투자액 배분이나 기업가치, 기술 평가 내용은 제공되지 않아 사업 전망을 추가로 판단하기는 어렵다.

articles.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
articles.content: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
articles.summary: 한 배우가 마이크로드라마 스타트업에 자신의 얼굴 사용권을 제공한 사례를 통해 AI 기반 배우 이미지 활용의 사업 모델을 다룬 기사다. 기사 설명은 이러한 흐름이 이미 중국에서 인기를 얻고 있으며, 할리우드로 확산될 경우 장기적 결과에 대한 전문가들의 우려가 있다고 전한다. 배우의 초상 활용과 콘텐츠 제작 사업의 관계를 보여주지만, 제공된 기록에는 사용 기술이나 계약 조건, 보상 구조가 없어 구체적인 권리 보호 수준은 확인할 수 없다.

articles.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
articles.content: Journalist Paris Marx unpacks his new book "Hyperscale."
articles.summary: 테크크런치는 언론인 패리스 마르크스의 신간 ‘Hyperscale’을 통해 데이터센터가 빅테크에 대한 반발의 중심에 놓인 이유를 다뤘다. 모델 성능이나 제품 출시보다는 대규모 컴퓨팅 인프라를 둘러싼 사회적 논쟁에 초점을 맞춘 기사다. 다만 제공된 설명에는 구체적인 반발 원인이나 사례, 수치가 없어 데이터센터 사업에 미칠 영향을 정량적으로 판단할 수 없다.

articles.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
articles.content: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
articles.summary: 테크크런치는 문자 메시지 안에서 이용할 수 있는 주요 AI 에이전트를 소개했다. 범용 비서뿐 아니라 가족, 여행, 업무에 특화된 에이전트도 포함해 메시징 인터페이스를 통한 활용 범위를 보여준다. 다만 제공된 기록에는 개별 제품명이나 기능·가격·권한 비교가 없어 실제 서비스 선택을 위한 구체적인 판단 근거는 부족하다.

articles.title: A tale of two Nvidias
articles.content: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia — the company’s latest earnings report vs. the tech executives loudly calling for Jensen Huang’s return.
articles.summary: 테크크런치는 엔비디아의 최신 실적 발표와 젠슨 황의 복귀를 공개적으로 요구하는 기술업계 경영진들의 목소리를 대비했다. 기업의 재무 발표와 업계 인사들의 요구가 서로 다른 모습을 보여준다는 것이 제공된 기사의 핵심 관점이다. 다만 실적 수치와 복귀 요구의 맥락이 제시되지 않아 엔비디아의 사업 성과나 경영 상황에 대한 구체적인 결론을 내릴 수 없다.
